scraped_articles.title: 1980 murder case: Allahabad HC finds two convicts were minors, remits matter to Juvenile Justice Board
scraped_articles.content:
Lucknow, The Allahabad High Court has set aside the sentences of two men convicted in a murder case 46 years ago after finding that both were minors at the time of the crime.
However, the Lucknow bench of the court upheld their conviction and referred the matter to the Juvenile Justice Board to determine the appropriate punishment.
A division bench of Justices Abdul Moin and Pramod Kumar Srivastava on Thursday passed the order on an appeal arising from the incident that took place in Sultanpur on September 28, 1980.
According to the prosecution, eight men attacked several persons with sharp-edged weapons and spears.
Four people - Shamshad, Abdul Rafiq, Dilsher and Hamidullah - were killed in the incident, while several others sustained injuries.
The sessions court had convicted all eight accused and sentenced them to life imprisonment on December 14, 1981.
During the pendency of their appeal in the high court, appellants Siraj Ahmad and Abdul Wahid claimed that they were minors when the incident occurred.
Following the high court's directions, the Juvenile Justice Board conducted an inquiry to ascertain their age.
Based on the board's report and educational records, the court found that Ahmad was 17 years and 10 months old, while Wahid was 17 years and 11 months old at the time of the crime.
While upholding their conviction, the bench observed that the testimonies of injured eyewitnesses and other witnesses were consistent with the medical evidence.
The prosecution had successfully established the charges, and there were no grounds to interfere with the findings of guilt.
However, the bench held that the sentences imposed under the criminal law could not be sustained in view of their juvenile status at the time of the offence.
The court observed that the two convicts could not be let off without any consequence, but the appropriate order had to be passed in accordance with the provisions of the juvenile justice law.
The bench directed both men to appear before the Juvenile Justice Board on October 28 along with a certified copy of the judgment. The board has been asked to pass an appropriate order within six weeks of receiving the certified copy.

scraped_articles.title: Pinarayi Vijayan moves SC against HC order to lodge FIR in CMRL bribery case
scraped_articles.content:
New Delhi, Former Keralam chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan on Friday moved the Supreme Court challenging a High Court of Kerala order to register an FIR in the alleged CMRL bribery case.
Sidharth Luthra, appearing for Vijayan, mentioned the plea for urgent listing before a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi, saying an FIR has been registered in the case.
Luthra also urged the bench to grant Vijayan protection from coercive action.
The CJI said the matter would be heard when the apex court re-opens on October 26 after the Dussehra break.
The CJI also said he may constitute a bench during the holidays next week, subject to the availability of judges.
In a setback to Vijayan and his kin, the Kerala High Court on Thursday dismissed their pleas to file appeals against a single-judge direction to lodge an FIR against them in the alleged CMRL bribery case.
A division bench of the high court rejected the applications of Vijayan, his daughter Veena T and her husband P A Mohamed Riyas to file an appeal against the single judge's October 9 order, while holding that "an accused in a corruption case has no legal right to be heard before registering the FIR".
It said that since the applications are dismissed, their appeals are also dismissed consequently.
Vijayan, Veena and Riyas, in their appeals before the division bench, had claimed that they were not heard by the single judge before issuing the October 9 direction to lodge the FIR.
The high court on October 9 directed the Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau to register a case based on a report submitted by the Enforcement Directorate to the state police.
The ED had sought registration of a case based on evidence gathered during its investigation and searches conducted under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act.
The agency has alleged that Cochin Minerals and Rutile Limited made fraudulent payments of ₹ 2.78 crore to Veena's now-defunct company, Exalogic Solutions, under the guise of IT consultancy services.

scraped_articles.title: Rajnath Singh accuses Congress of seeking ‘regime change through violence’ amid anti-CEC protests
scraped_articles.content:
Union defence minister Rajnath Singh on Friday targeted the Congress party over its recent protests against chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, saying that it wants “regime change by unleashing violence” in the country.
"Congress wants to follow the Bangladesh model of violence for regime change. Congress protest is not against Gyanesh Kumar and SIR but against democracy to topple government," he said during a press conference in Lucknow.
Singh accused the Congress of turning the Election Commission into its “puppet” while in power.
"In 1993, Congress made overnight changes in the EC. The then Chief EC had recommended to the President of India that the then EC, Naveen Chawla, be removed. But Congress elevated him to the post of Chief Election Commissioner," Singh said.
"Before 1993, there was no voter ID card. There was nothing to prove voters' identity. After voter ID was rolled out, Congress has not been able to form a government on its own," he said.
The minister alleged that the Congress' protests against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) and CEC Gyanesh Kumar were not about electoral rolls but an “attempt to weaken institutions” that function independently.
He said Lok Sabha LoP and Congress MP Rahul Gandhi needed to understand that democracy did not give anyone the right to resort to violence. "Rahul is doing the politics of disruption," Singh added.

scraped_articles.title: Ammo deal graft probe casts shadow on top-performing defence PSU, clean-up on cards
scraped_articles.content:
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into an alleged corruption case linked to a ₹ 500-crore ammunition contract has cast a shadow over Munitions India Limited (MIL), one of the defence ministry’s best-performing ordnance units which has also strengthened its presence in overseas markets.
MIL is set to face a clean-up and a renewed push for accountability following the corruption allegations, officials familiar with the matter said. The department of defence production is tracking the case closely, the officials added.
MIL executive director Anil Kumar, his brother B Harshavardhan and SMPP Limited CEO Ashish Kansal were arrested on Wednesday.
Also Read: CBI to examine all recent contracts awarded by arrested official amid ₹ 500 crore ammunition deal bribery case
According to official data, MIL posted a profit after tax of ₹ 1,250 crore in 2025-26, the highest among the seven defence companies carved out of the erstwhile Ordnance Factory Board (OFB) five years ago.
The seven firms, including Advanced Weapons and Equipment India Limited, Troop Comforts Limited, India Optel Limited, Avani Armoured Vehicles, Gliders India Limited and Yantra India Limited, together posted a profit of ₹ 2,801 crore, the data shows.
MIL reported record revenue of ₹ 10,954 crore in 2025-26, up 33% from the previous year. The Pune-headquartered company manufactures a wide range of ammunition, including tank ammunition, bombs and rockets. It has secured export orders worth ₹ 1,500 crore for 28 products across nine countries.
The OFB’s corporatisation was aimed at boosting its efficiency and competitiveness in a long-awaited reform in the country’s defence manufacturing sector.
SMPP Limited could face suspension or a ban on government business dealings under the Centre’s rules for procuring weapons and systems following the graft charges, as HT first reported. The department of defence production is expected to decide on possible action against the firm. SMPP manufactures ammunition, loitering munitions, bullet-proof jackets and helmets.
The Defence Procurement Manual states that the competent authority may impose financial penalties and/or suspend or ban business dealings with an entity if it resorts to corrupt practices, unfair means , or illegal activities at any stage to secure a contract, even when a PCIP (pre-contract integrity pact) is not mandated.
Violation of the PCIP is also a key ground for initiating action.
The manual adds that the competent authority may suspend business dealings with an entity pending a full inquiry into allegations or facts relating to any ground for punitive action. The government may suspend business dealings with an entity when it refers any complaint against it to the CBI or any investigating agency or when it receives intimation regarding the initiation of a criminal investigation or inquiry against any entity.
The period of suspension ordinarily does not exceed one year. In exceptional cases and those involving national security, the government may order a longer ban.

scraped_articles.title: Manipur: Kuki body demands probe into killing of woman in Kamjong district
scraped_articles.content:
Kuki-Zo Council (KZC), a Kuki Zo body, on Friday condemned the killing of a woman of the community allegedly by cadres of National Socialist Council of Nagaland-Issac Muivah (NSCN-IM) faction in Manipur’s Kamjong district a day earlier and demanded an impartial investigation into the incident.
According to a statement issued by KZC, four Kuki-Zo villagers were travelling from Molvailup to Phaikoh to purchase essential commodities when they were reportedly ambushed by NSCN-IM cadres at around 4pm on Thursday.
During the incident, one Hatneikim Haokip, was killed at the spot, while her husband, identified as Jamkhogam Haokip, sustained serious injuries, the council said.
The council claimed that the incident brought the reported death toll of Kuki-Zo civilians killed in the violence attributed to NSCN-IM and Zeliangrong United Front- Kamson [ZUF(K)] faction to 30. The council demanded an immediate and impartial investigation to book those responsible for the act.
Also Read: Kuki Man found dead after alleged abduction by armed group in Manipur’s Kangpokpi district
“If Naga leaders in Manipur are demanding the abrogation of the Suspension of Operations (SoO) agreements with KNO/UPF, the ceasefire arrangement with NSCN -IM must also be reviewed for abrogation. The same standards must apply to all armed groups, without discrimination or political favouritism,” the KZC said in the statement.
“The government must uphold the rule of law through consistent and impartial action. It cannot apply different standards to different groups while overlooking allegations of grave violence against the Kuki-Zo people. Justice cannot be selective, and accountability must be equal for all,” Kuki-Zo Council said.

scraped_articles.title: IAS officer abuses colleague, threatens suspension after she objects: 'I can talk like that, I'm your boss'
scraped_articles.content:
A senior Indian Administrative Service officer has sparked a controversy after a video of him abusing a junior woman officer and threatening to recommend her suspension went viral on social media.
The incident took place over a virtual review meeting on Mission YUVA, wherein a heated argument ensued between Jammu &Kashmir IAS officer Rajeev Ranjan and Beenish Wani, a 2015-batch JKAS officer, over the role of National Rural Livelihood Mission (NRLM). Wani is assistant director of employment and counselling centre, Ganderbal, while Ranjan is currently posted as administrative secretary, labour and employment in J&K.
During the meeting, Ranjan, a 2010 batch IAS officer, was heard calling Wani “stupid”, while also using abusive words like “bl***y sh*t”.
Also Read | Omar set to expand J&K cabinet in balancing act
A video of the review meeting shows Ranjan allegedly interrupting Wani when she was briefing the meeting about the targets achieved by her office, according to a news agency PTI report.
While Wani, who was attending the meeting via video conferencing, was trying to explain that NRLM was used as a helping agency to achieve targets, Ranjan was heard saying, “Why do you need NRLM? If NRLM had to do this work, why would I give it to AD (assistant director)?” He continued further, saying, “If someone else had to do the work, do you just have to write the letter? And you want a medal for it?”
When Wani tried to reply, saying NRLM would “need to help us”, Ranjan was heard telling her to “shut up," and asking her whether she would sit silently or not. “Sir let me speak. You're not letting me explain myself,” Wani was heard telling the IAS officer.

As the argument unfolded, Ranjan called the woman officer “bl***y sh*t”. “I can always talk like that. I am your boss, stupid,” he said. When the female officer objected to Ranjan's language and said he could not call her “sh*t”, he asked another woman officer to type out her suspension order. He further yelled at Wani, telling her to “get out.” Wani said they can suspend her, while adding, “To h*ll with you.”
“Record this and immediately suspend, and write to the GD how she should be thrown out of this service. Record this now, the suspension must go now,” Ranjan was then heard telling the other woman officer.
Following the incident, the Jammu and Kashmir Administrative Service (JKAS) fraternity called for an impartial inquiry into the incident, and urged Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha, Chief Secretary Atal Dullo, and the General Administration Department to ensure that no retaliatory action is taken against Wani.
The fraternity said that while it upholds administrative accountability, it maintains that no supervising authority can use abusive language and intimidation. The fraternity further alleged that the senior officer had a pattern of using “unparliamentary and demeaning language” in official capacity. They said that the department's attempt to dismiss the circulating video as AI-generated was “more disturbing.”
“The video is authentic, as testified by the officer herself and other officials who were present during the virtual meeting,” the JKAS fraternity asserted.

scraped_articles.title: Andhra Police arrest two more in Pak-linked ''espionage'' case
scraped_articles.content:
Amaravati, Two more persons have been arrested in connection with the alleged espionage conspiracy involving Pakistani Intelligence Operatives , police said on Thursday.
The arrested were identified as Bongu Ravi and Kadari Srinivas.
"The Andhra Pradesh Police Counter Intelligence Cell has apprehended two additional persons in the espionage case involving PIOs, bringing the total number of arrests to four," an intelligence official told PTI.
The investigation revealed that an unidentified woman using the name 'Angel Payal' allegedly contacted Ravi, an employee of an engineering company at the Naval Dockyard in Visakhapatnam, through Facebook in 2023, claiming to work for a Dubai-based shipping firm.
She allegedly induced Ravi to share details about ships and submarines at the naval dockyard in exchange for money. Ravi and Srinivas, his colleague, allegedly colluded and shared information about the number of ships and submarines at the restricted defence establishment with the woman, the official added.
Ravi allegedly received money from the woman into his bank account and subsequently paid a share to Srinivas, the investigation revealed.
The case was registered at Malkapuram Police Station in Visakhapatnam on October 12, 2025, under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Official Secrets Act, 1923.
Ravi was arrested and remanded to judicial custody, while a Look Out Circular was initiated against Srinivas, who had left India for Saudi Arabia on October 11, 2025.
The Andhra Pradesh Counter Intelligence Cell, in coordination with central intelligence agencies, traced Srinivas, who was intercepted at the Delhi airport on October 11, 2026, while returning from Saudi Arabia. He was brought to Malkapuram Police Station for examination, the official said.
A charge sheet had earlier been filed against Ravi, the unidentified woman and Srinivas before the jurisdictional court, while further investigation is underway.
On October 6, the Andhra Pradesh Police Counter Intelligence Cell arrested two persons, including a naval staffer, for allegedly spying for Pakistan. Out of the 18 suspects in the case, 13 are naval personnel.
The investigation involves suspected attempts to obtain sensitive defence information through fake social media identities, honeytrapping, monetary inducements and WhatsApp activation OTPs.

scraped_articles.title: K’taka cabinet rejects mercy pleas of convicts in 2003 techie murder
scraped_articles.content:
The Karnataka Cabinet on Thursday rejected the clemency petitions of Shubha Shankaranarayana and D Arun Verma, who are serving life sentences for the December 2003 murder of Shubha’s fiance, software engineer B V Girish, in Bengaluru.
The Cabinet held that the killing was premeditated and exceptionally brutal, and that the pleas could not be accepted under the applicable legal framework.
“It (clemency plea) has been rejected because there is no scope in the law for it. We had taken an opinion from the Law Department before placing the matter before the Cabinet. The recommendation will now be sent to Governor Sudha Yadav for a final decision on the petitions,” home minister Priyank Kharge told reporters after the cabinet meeting.
The petitions followed a July 14, 2025, Supreme Court judgment upholding the life sentences of all four convicts. The court had given them eight weeks to approach the Governor under Article 161 of the Constitution, which empowers Governors to grant pardons, remit sentences or commute punishments in matters within a state’s executive jurisdiction.
The Governor will take the final decision on the petitions.
Girish, 27, worked with Intel in Bengaluru. Shubha, then 20, was studying law at BMS Law College. The two got engaged on December 1, 2003, and were scheduled to marry on April 11, 2004. According to the prosecution, Shubha wanted to pursue her relationship with Verma, a fellow law student, and did not wish to marry Girish.
On December 3, Shubha took Girish out for dinner and later accompanied him to an aircraft viewing point on Airport Ring Road. There, an assailant struck him on the head with a steel rod. Girish was taken to Manipal Hospital, where he died the following morning.
Investigators later arrested Shubha, Verma and two other men, A Venkatesh and Dinesh, also known as Dinakaran.
The Supreme Court examined communications between the accused, including 38 text messages exchanged between Shubha and Verma between 6.37pm and 9.39pm on the evening of the murder. The court considered these records alongside other evidence to establish the conspiracy.
A trial court convicted all four in July 2010 and sentenced them to life imprisonment. The Karnataka High Court upheld the sentences later that year. The Supreme Court subsequently examined their appeals and, on July 14, 2025, confirmed the convictions and life sentences.

scraped_articles.title: ED files charge sheet against FIITJEE, two directors over fee fraud
scraped_articles.content:
The Enforcement Directorate (ED) on Thursday filed a charge sheet against coaching institute FIITJEE Limited and its directors, Dinesh Kumar Goel and Monila Goel, alleging that they laundered ₹ 85.79 crore collected as advance fees from students for coaching programmes that were not delivered.
The central agency’s Lucknow zonal office filed the prosecution complaint before a special Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) court in Ghaziabad, seeking the conviction of the company and the two directors, along with the confiscation of assets worth ₹ 71.88 crore seized or attached during the investigation, ED said in a statement.
ED’s money laundering case stems from four police FIRs -- two each filed by Uttar Pradesh Police in Noida and Madhya Pradesh Police in Bhopal -- alleging that the coaching institute collected fees of ₹ 2.8 lakh to ₹ 3.5 lakh per student in advance for two-to-four-year coaching programmes for competitive examinations such as Joint Entrance Examination (JEE) for the IITs on the assurance that the full programme would be delivered.
However, according to the ED, the faculty left due to “unpaid” salaries and the centres closed “abruptly” without prior notice.
ED alleged that its probe found that FIITJEE abruptly closed 32 centres in Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh between May 2024 and February 2025, leaving 14,411 enrolled students without the coaching they had paid for. Despite the closures and faculty departures over unpaid salaries, the company continued enrolling students for programmes running until March 2029, it said.
The collected fees were spent while the company operated at a continuous deficit, the agency claimed.
HT tried to reach out to the company on a number listed on its website but the number does not exist.
Directors drew ₹ 24.92 crore in salaries
ED alleged that Dinesh and Monila Goel drew a combined ₹ 24.92 crore in salaries from the financial year 2022-23 onwards, even as salaries of employees were delayed or remained unpaid.
Dinesh drew about ₹ 56 lakh a month, while Monila received more than ₹ 25 lakh a month, the agency said, adding that the Goel family held 86.31% of the company’s shares, allowing the directors to approve their own remuneration without independent checks.
According to ED, Monila told investigators that she did not attend the office regularly and signed cheques from home. Payments to her continued even as the coaching centres were closing.
Noida Police had earlier filed a charge sheet naming both directors as accused, based on statements from around 300 victims, coaching centre operators and other witnesses, along with fee receipts and other evidence, the ED said.
The agency searched seven premises on April 24, 2025, seizing ₹ 10 lakh in cash and jewellery worth ₹ 4.86 crore. It subsequently provisionally attached properties worth ₹ 66.92 crore on October 9, 2026, under the PMLA.
ED said further investigation is underway.

scraped_articles.title: Dushyant Gautam’s gubernatorial role puts Uttarakhand BJP in a bind amid Ankita Bhandari murder row
scraped_articles.content:
Dushyant Gautam’s appointment as the governor of Sikkim has caused ripples in poll-bound Uttarakhand, where the Congress has trained its guns at the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party, alleging it is trying to “shield” the leader whose name cropped up in the 19-year-old Anika Bhandari’s murder case in 2022.
On Thursday, while the BJP leadership backed Gautam, asserting there was no evidence against him, several leaders in the state expressed concern that the issue could cast a shadow on the party’s election campaign.
Uttarakhand goes to the polls early next year, and the BJP has been in power since 2017.
The BJP has officially maintained that there is no evidence against Gautam, a Dalit face of the BJP who was a Rajya Sabha MP and a national general secretary. Gautam also filed a defamation case against the Congress and the Aam Aadmi Party for alleging his involvement after video and audio clips surfaced where the partner of former BJP MLA Suresh Rathore alleged that a "VIP" was linked to the crime.
There was an insinuation that the VIP was Gautam.
“The state government had taken swift steps to arrest the accused and set up a special investigation team to probe the crime. The anger and concern over the case, since it involved a young girl, didn’t become a political issue the way it has after his (Gautam’s) appointment (as Governor),” said a leader speaking on condition of anonymity.
He said the appointment will be used by the Congress as a “political tool”.
“You could say, the appointment has rekindled the memories of the crime. The issue will resonate more with the women in particular, and we cannot offend that key constituency. In the hill region, women play a key role in shaping opinions,” said the leader quoted above.
A second leader said the party will need a sharp and effective counter to the Congress’ allegations and the demand that Gautam’s appointment be withheld until the court-monitored CBI probe is concluded. The party leaders fear that the allegation that the gubernatorial post is a ruse to “provide immunity” to Gautam from persecution could resonate among youngsters drawn to social media.
“The absence of protests on the ground does not necessarily mean that the issue has no traction…” the second leader said.
The first leader quoted above said Gautam’s appointment has another downside: it comes at a time when the Upper Castes are up in arms with the government over the University Grants Commission (UGC) equity regulation (challenged in court), and there is a perception that the government is overlooking the general categories.
“BJP’s push for social engineering does not have the same impact in Uttarakhand as it does in states such as Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. Of the four governors who were appointed last week, two Gautam and Mohan Ram (Odisha) are SCs. So, there is a perception that UCs are being overlooked. Earlier, Ajay Tamta (Lok Sabha MP) was made minister in the Union Council; then Dinesh Arya was sent to the Rajya Sabha,” the leader said.
The largest caste group in the state are the Upper Castes, the Rajputs/Thakurs, who are estimated to be 35% of the state's total population, followed by Brahmins, who are approximately 25%. Scheduled Castes are estimated at about 18%, the leader said.

scraped_articles.title: Defence company may face ban over arrest of CEO for bribery
scraped_articles.content:
Defence firm SMPP Limited could face a suspension or a ban on government business dealings under the Centre’s rules for procuring weapons and systems following the arrest of its CEO and two others by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) in an alleged bribery case, officials familiar with the matter said on Thursday.
SMPP CEO Ashish Kansal, state-owned Munitions India Limited (MIL) executive director Anil Kumar and his brother B Harshavardhan were held on Wednesday in a case linked to a ₹ 500-crore ammunition deal.
The department of defence production is expected to decide the possible action against the firm, the officials added, asking not to be named. SMPP manufactures ammunition, loitering munitions, bullet-proof jackets and helmets.
SMPP did not respond to a query from HT on the developments. There was no official response from the defence ministry either.
The allegations include Kumar disclosing sensitive information concerning defence production, procurement and other important activities of MIL. CBI officials said they recovered ₹ 1.73 crore in cash during a raid on Kumar’s premises in Pune. The investigating agency also seized ₹ 50 lakh in cash, along with incriminating documents, during searches in Mysuru and Bengaluru in Karnataka and Delhi.
Rules state that the competent authority may impose financial penalties and/or suspend or ban business dealings with an entity if the firm resorts to corrupt practices, unfair means, or illegal activities at any stage to secure a contract, even when a PCIP (pre-contract integrity pact) is not mandated.
Violation of the PCIP is also a key ground for initiating action.
The manual states that the competent authority may suspend business dealings with an entity pending a full inquiry into allegations or facts relating to any ground for punitive action. The government may suspend business dealings with an entity when it refers any complaint against it to the CBI or any investigating agency or when it receives intimation regarding the initiation of a criminal investigation or inquiry against any entity.
The manual details the outcome of suspending business dealings with a firm.
“An order of suspension of business dealings with an entity shall result in immediate ineligibility of the entity from participating in future bids. No RFP (request for proposal) will be issued to such an entity. An order suspending business dealings with an entity may extend to its allied firms,” according to the manual.
The period of suspension ordinarily does not exceed one year. In exceptional cases and those involving national security, the government may order a longer ban.
The entity whose business dealings are suspended or banned may participate in future RFPs for spares, upgrades and maintenance of the equipment/weapon systems it supplied earlier, if that equipment is a proprietary item and no alternative sources of supply are available, the manual adds.
MIL was one of the seven defence companies carved out of the erstwhile Ordnance Factory Board (OFB) five years ago. The state-owned firm faces a clean-up and an accountability push following the corruption allegations. The board’s corporatisation was aimed at boosting its efficiency and competitiveness in a long-awaited reform in the country’s defence manufacturing sector.

scraped_articles.title: CBI to examine all recent contracts awarded by arrested official amid  ₹500 crore ammunition deal bribery case
scraped_articles.content:
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) will examine all recent contracts awarded by Munitions India Limited (MIL) executive director Anil Kumar, who was arrested earlier this week for allegedly conniving with private contractors to extend favours to them at the state-run defence company in exchange for bribes, people familiar with the development said.
Officials said they will write to the defence ministry as well as MIL management to seek files or contracts handled by Kumar “to see the links between procurement decisions, private vendors and payments”.
He is currently being interrogated by the agency's sleuths, as allegations include leaking sensitive information related to defence production and procurement in exchange for bribes.
“MIL’s contracts are sensitive and important for the country's security. We will look into all the defence contracts handled by Kumar at MIL,” said an officer, who asked not to be named.
CBI had received information that huge amounts of cash were being delivered through ‘hawala’ to Kumar at his residence in Pune, after which a raid was carried out, and he was taken into custody on Wednesday.
Officials said that during interrogation, it was learnt that the cash was the bribe amount for favouring SMPP Limited in a ₹ 500 crore ammunition deal.
SMPP’s CEO Ashish Kansal and Kumar’s brother B Harshvardhan have also been arrested. The agency recovered ₹ 1.73 crore cash from Kumar’s premises and another ₹ 50 lakh from further raids at various locations in Mysuru, Bengaluru and Delhi.
The agency has alleged that Kumar was demanding and accepting illegal gratification from private contractors and vendors in exchange for official favours and the disclosure of sensitive information concerning defence production, procurement, and other strategically important activities of the company.
The agency has invoked sections pertaining to criminal conspiracy under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and sections pertaining to the Prevention of Corruption Act.

scraped_articles.title: Delhi: Customs officials seize 148 kg of suspected cannabis hidden in plastic spools
scraped_articles.content:
Customs officers at the Air Cargo Complex in Delhi foiled a major smuggling attempt after intercepting a consignment from Bangkok containing 148.67 kg of suspected cannabis concealed inside plastic spools, a release said on Thursday.
The operation was conducted by officers of the Special Intelligence and Investigation Branch (SIIB) following locally developed intelligence, according to a press release issued by the Office of the Principal Commissioner of Customs.
The consignment had been declared as PU tubes and packed in 19 cartons. It was placed on hold after officers suspected a misdeclaration. During an examination conducted in the presence of the importer's representative, officers discovered plastic spools containing the consignment. When the spools were opened, hidden cavities revealed packets of compacted green substance wrapped in polythene. Such packets were found in 15 cartons.
Preliminary diagnostic tests indicated that the seized material was ganja or marijuana.
The customs department stated that a total of 120 spools concealed 148.67 kg of suspected hydroponic weed. The seized substance was valued at approximately ₹ 52 crore, while its estimated street value in India was put at ₹ 150 crore.
The suspected narcotics, along with the concealment and packaging materials, were seized under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985.
The operation lasted more than 72 hours and culminated in the arrest of one person on Thursday, October 15. The individual was produced before a magistrate on the same day.
Follow-up searches at five premises across three states have provided further leads for the ongoing investigation, the press release stated. The operation was monitored by senior customs officers at the levels of the Chief Commissioner and Principal Commissioner, ACC Imports, and supervised by the Additional Commissioner of Customs, ACC Imports.
The department said that further investigation was in progress, adding that customs officers remained vigilant and committed to protecting society from the threat of narcotics.

scraped_articles.title: Dead fish in Yamuna near Burari raise alarm over Delhi river’s water quality
scraped_articles.content:
Several dead fish have been spotted along the Yamuna near Burari in north Delhi since Wednesday night, raising concerns over the river’s water quality and possible industrial pollution. Wildlife experts and activists have flagged the incident, citing the possibility of untreated industrial effluents and low dissolved oxygen levels.
Wildlife enthusiast and conservationist Hemant Garg, who spotted the dead fish on Wednesday, said, “We regularly go in Yamuna to wildlife conservation, bird census and tracking wildlife. The fish were observed last night and thousands of dead fish have been seen way upstream up to shank number 10, 11 and 12. The water usually clean here. We should be wary as drinking water is also sourced from this part of river.”
Ranjan Mukhia, a boatman in Burari, said that the water has a strong stench and the fish deaths are not restricted to this stretch alone. “We have our fellow boatmen upstream who have reported that dead fish have been seen upstream in Haryana as well. We have to remove dead fish to ensure water doesn’t get even more polluted with carcasses,” he said.
Bhim Singh Rawat, a Yamuna activist and member of the South Asia Network on Dams, Rivers and People (SANDRP), said that such mass fish mortality incidents are usually reported in summer months when high temperatures lead to lower levels of dissolved oxygen.
“We cant recall the last such episode in winter months. The possibility in this case could be untreated industrial effluents. There is drain number 2 from Panipat, drain number 8 and one drain in Burari which may have discharged large amounts of untreated industrial effluents,” Rawat said. “The flow in the river has been restricted despite monsoonal flow,” he added.
Yamuna activist Pankaj Kumar wrote to the Delhi Pollution Control Committee, seeking urgent intervention.
“Fish mortality is critical bio indicator of severe ecological stress the primary causes are low dissolved oxygen, high biochemical oxygen demand and presence of toxic industrial effluents. If toxic substances are present in river in sufficient quantity to kill fish, the same water being abstracted downstream at Wazirabad for drinking purposes poses direct health risk to public health,” he said.
The New Delhi Nature Society, in a post on X, said, “Hundreds, maybe thousands, of fish found dead on 14th October in the Yamuna river near Burari, Delhi. Specific cause not established. Locals allege chemical waste discharged from Haryana through canals. Could it be related to the acid rain on Oct 12th?”
In May 2026, hundreds of fish died at Sanjay Lake in east Delhi amid a heatwave and receding water levels. Experts pointed to a combination of high temperatures, concentrated pollutants and declining dissolved oxygen, which can make aquatic conditions lethal for fish. Earlier, in April 2026, thousands of dead fish surfaced in Delhi’s Najafgarh drain, with locals reporting that industrial effluents from Haryana were a likely cause.
In May 2025 and, before that, in July 2024, hundreds of dead fish were recorded along the Yamuna banks near Burari in north Delhi.
The monthly Yamuna water quality report for September shows that, despite the monsoon season, the river stretch in Delhi failed to show significant improvement or dilution of pollutants. A comparison of the water quality reports for September 2025 and September 2026 shows that the biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) and faecal coliform levels were much higher at several locations along the river.
At Palla, the faecal coliform level this year was 1,100 units (MPN/200 ml), compared with 790 units last year. At the ISBT Bridge, it was recorded at 35,000 units, compared with 2,800 units last year. At Okhla barrage, faecal coliform levels of 21,000 units were recorded —six times higher than the 3,500 units recorded in September last year. Faecal coliform is an indicator of untreated sewage in the water. The level should ideally be below 500 units, with a maximum limit of 2,500 units.
At ISBT Bridge, BOD was 30 mg/l this year, compared with 8 mg/l on September 3 last year. Chemical oxygen demand (COD) rose from 44 mg/l to 92 mg/l over the same period. A BOD level of 3 mg/l or less and dissolved oxygen of at least 5 mg/l are specified for bathing. At ITO Bridge, BOD climbed from 4 mg/l to 18 mg/l, while COD rose from 20 mg/l to 60 mg/l. Faecal coliform levels increased from 1,800 to 17,000 MPN/100 ml.

scraped_articles.title: Kuki woman killed, two missing after gunfight breaks out in Manipur’s Kamjong
scraped_articles.content:
A woman from the Kuki community was reportedly killed and two others went missing following a gunfight between Kuki and Naga groups in Manipur’s Kamjong district on Thursday, police said, amid continuing tensions between the two communities.
Police officers said the incident occurred at around 4 pm in the jungle between Phaikoh and Mulvailup villages, close to the Indo-Myanmar border.
Also Read I 9 killed as Naga-Kuki clashes flare in 3 Manipur districts in 24 hours
Local Kuki bodies claimed that Hatneikim Haokip (age could be confirmed) was killed during the crossfire, while her husband managed to escape unhurt. Two other Kuki-Zo civilians remain missing, they said.
Hatneikim Haokip and three others were reportedly travelling to purchase essential commodities for their families when the attack was allegedly launched by suspected members of the National Socialist Council of Nagaland-Isak Muivah (NSCN-IM), a Naga militant group.
However, the allegation could not be independently verified.
Five days ago, on October 10, two Tangkhul Naga village guards were gunned down in Ningchou Naga village by suspected Kuki-based militant groups who had infiltrated from across the Myanmar border.
Police officers said that on the same day, two other Kuki civilians, including a 42-year-old woman, were also killed during crossfire between armed militants and security forces.
Four members of the Naga community were also killed on September 25 in Pilong village in Kamjong district. The police FIR mentioned that “some unidentified armed persons suspected to be a rebel group of Myanmar base militant (KNA(B) holding sophisticated persons entered Pilong village along with the Indo-Myanmar and opened fire upon the villagers.”
The Naga-Kuki tensions intensified following twin ambushes on May 13 that left four people, including three church leaders, dead. In the aftermath of the ambushes, 48 people were taken hostage, triggering protests, shutdowns and a blockade along all three national highways in the state.
The ethnic clashes in Manipur first began between the Meitei and Kuki communities before involving almost every community. The state’s Meitei and Kuki-Zo communities have shut each other out from the areas they dominate since the ethnic clashes began in May 2023, leaving at least 260 people dead and displacing 60,000.
Also Read I Manipur shutdown disrupts normal life as KCP-Apunba marks merger with India as ‘Black Day’
The Meiteis, mostly Hindu, live largely in the Imphal Valley. The Kukis, predominantly Christian, reside in the hills. The state government has maintained that there are no buffer zones dividing communities in the state, but it has identified certain sensitive areas.
A new government was formed in February, nearly a year after the imposition of President’s Rule. It includes representatives from all three major communities as part of an attempt to maintain ethnic balance.

scraped_articles.title: Supreme Court to issue orders on preventive steps taken by Centre to curb online child sexual abuse content
scraped_articles.content:
The Supreme Court on Thursday agreed to issue orders on preventive steps to be taken by the Centre and other stakeholders against child sexual exploitative and abuse material (CSEAM) online, citing the seriousness of the matter.
The order was passed after the ministry of electronics and information technology (MeitY) submitted a draft Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) to the court. “As part of the future preventive action required to be taken with respect to dissemination of CSEAM content, MeitY has drafted an SOP for the intermediaries for prevention, direction, removal and reporting of CSEAM content to a government portal (Sahyog),” the ministry said.
Also Read I US coach who recorded young gymnasts undressing is sentenced to 90 years in prison
The SOP has been prepared in consultation with the ministry of women and child development (MoWCD) and other stakeholders, besides the ministry of home affairs (MHA) and department of telecommunications (DoT), the affidavit said.
Solicitor general Tushar Mehta appearing for Centre said, “We are serious about this matter. There were discussions that took place based on which we have given our suggestions on how to tackle this problem. We require some more time to finalise the SOP.”
The bench said, “This is a very serious matter. We want the Union government to take it seriously. We will pass an order. You study our order. We will suggest you some things that will be helpful for you.”
The court posted the matter after a month to allow the Centre come up with further developments on preventing CSEAM online.
The Centre’s affidavit gave examples of how in an instance, MeitY issued notice in July 2026 to the Meta’s compliance officer regarding dissemination of paid advertisements promoting CSEAM. The proceedings are still underway. Meity said it has been regularly communicating and coordinating with various stakeholders, including the intermediaries, regarding the need for enhanced monitoring, reporting and removal of CSEAM content.
As part of these efforts, Centre pointed out that in February this year, the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 were amended to incorporate specific due diligence obligations for preventing and reporting CSEAM content on their platforms.
The Centre was responding to an order passed by the court last month in a petition filed by Just Rights for Children Alliance (JRCA). The petitioner sought compliance of a 2024 judgment and a uniform SOP to be framed to ensure timely reporting by intermediaries.
The judgment passed on September 23, 2024 held that social media intermediaries have a duty to report cases of child abuse and exploitation to the local authorities under Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (Pocso) Act.
The verdict held, “In view of the salutary object and the mandatory character of the provisions of Sections 19 and 20 of the Pocso read with Rule 11 of the Pocso Rules, we are of the considered view, that an intermediary cannot claim exemption from the liability under Section 79 of the IT Act for any third-party information, data, or communication link made available or hosted by it, unless due diligence is conducted by it and compliance is made of these provisions of the Pocso.”
It further stated that the compliance required includes not just removal of child pornographic content but an immediate report of such content to the concerned police.
Also Read I Gabrielle Hanson and Jacob Randolph: San José parents charged with neglect as daughter, 8, dies in cockroach-infested home
The JRCA application said that Instagram carried paid advertisements promoting CSEAM, raising concerns over compliance of the top court’s judgment. The petitioner sought a comprehensive mechanism to ensure effective implementation of obligations of social media platforms and prevent the online circulation and exploitation of children. It sought a uniform SOP for intermediaries covering detection and mandatory reporting of CSEAM, preservation of evidence and inter-agency coordination among relevant agencies.
It further demanded prompt uploading of offenders’ particulars to the National Database of Sexual Offenders (NDSO), timely action by law-enforcement agencies on every report received from an intermediary, and initiation of criminal proceedings against intermediaries that fail to comply with mandatory reporting obligations, in accordance with law.
The petitioner even sought the establishment of a centralised online reporting portal to facilitate reporting of CSEAM by intermediaries.

scraped_articles.title: Assam University assistant professor booked for molesting woman researcher in Bengaluru: Police
scraped_articles.content:
An assistant professor at Assam University in Silchar was booked for allegedly molesting a woman researcher during a conference held in Bengaluru, police said.
The woman researcher lodged a complaint at the Assam University police outpost on October 11, alleging sexual harassment, Cachar senior superintendent of police (SSP) Partha Pratim Das said. “We received a complaint and we are probing it,” Das said.
He added that the matter involves a central university and that, under the Vishaka guidelines, the university’s internal investigation report is important before the police intervene.
Registrar of Assam University, Silchar (AUS), Pradosh Kiran Nath, said that the woman researcher lodged a complaint alleging molestation around October 7, and the matter was referred to the Internal Complaints Committee (ICC).
“We held a meeting, and the ICC has been asked to complete the investigation as soon as possible and submit its report,” he said, adding that the university has a strict policy on sexual harassment.
The woman researcher told HT on Thursday that the incident occurred during an international academic conference held in Bengaluru in September and that she was subsequently threatened by the assistant professor several times.
“On the night of September 26, after an academic discussion, the supervisor insisted on accompanying me to my allotted room. We were alone at the lift when he made an inappropriate personal proposition and asked me to engage in physical intimacy. When I refused, he said that it could have adverse consequences for my academic progress,” she said.
She said that she later contacted her fiance and sought help from two female faculty members from other universities. “The two faculty members extended their support and stayed with me that night,” she added.
She alleged that the assistant professor from the department of performing arts later began creating obstacles in her academic progress and that she was denied information about two Research Advisory Committee (RAC) meetings.
“He threatened to create difficulties for me and said he would not let me complete my PhD. He also said that my research work would not progress unless I complied with his instructions,” she said.
HT reached out to the assistant professor accused of molestation, but his official contact number remained switched off until the report was filed.
Registrar Nath said that the assistant professor attended an online meeting last week and that the ICC was examining his attendance after the complaint was lodged.
Assam University has witnessed similar incidents in the past as well, and the registrar said that strict action had been taken against the accused in those cases.

scraped_articles.title: Woman can face gang rape charge without personally committing the act, says Delhi HC
scraped_articles.content:
The Delhi high court on Friday held that a woman can be charged with the offence of gang rape even if she has not personally committed the act of rape.
A bench of justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani observed that there was no rationale or basis to interpret the phrase “one or more persons constituting a group” in the provision on gang rape as referring exclusively to men. The court said the term “persons” must instead be interpreted in a “gender-neutral” manner.
“In the opinion of this court, this is significant, since for purposes of the offence of gang rape it is not necessary that a person acting in furtherance of a common intention must also be amongst the persons who physically commit the offence of rape. For instance, a woman who may not be part of the group of persons who commit the physical offence of rape may yet have acted in furtherance of a common intention to have rape committed upon the victim,” the court said.
It added, “As a sequitur to the above, this court is of the view that there is no basis to hold that a woman cannot be charged with the offence of gang rape under section 376D of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and section 70 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). It is, however, necessary to clarify that a woman alone cannot be charged with the offence of gang rape since that would prima-facié not be in conformity with the statutory definition of rape as it appears even in the post-2013 section 375 of IPC and section 63 of BNS, as currently construed.”
The court passed the order while dealing with a petition filed by the mother of a minor survivor, challenging a trial court’s January 17, 2025, order charging her under sections 70(2) (gang rape of a woman under 18 years of age), 351(3) (criminal intimidation) and 64(2)(m) (aggravated rape) of the BNS, and section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act.
In the present case, the minor survivor’s mother had filed an FIR in July 2024, alleging that her daughter had been kidnapped. In her statement, the minor said that her mother had threatened that if she did not have physical relations with the accused, he would kill her. She also alleged that her mother had forced her to have such relations and was present during the incidents of sexual assault.
In her petition before the high court, the mother asserted that she could not be charged with the offence of gang rape. It was also contended that only a ‘man’ could commit rape, that the offence of ‘gang rape’ could only be committed by a ‘group of men’, and that a woman could never be charged with that offence.
Amicus curiae Rohan J Alva submitted that Section 63 of the BNS envisages the possibility of rape being committed by a woman or a non-male offender, as the provision is no longer confined to penile-vaginal penetration. He further argued that Section 63 aims to protect women from all forms of sexual assault and that, since it recognises acts of penetration beyond penile-vaginal penetration as rape, there is no rational basis to restrict the offence’s applicability to male offenders alone.
The Delhi Police adopted Alva’s submissions.
Consequently, the court dismissed the petition and upheld the trial court’s order.

scraped_articles.title: Karnataka Cabinet rejects mercy pleas of fiancé, her partner in 2003 Bengaluru techie murder case
scraped_articles.content:
The Karnataka Cabinet on Thursday rejected mercy petitions filed by Shubha Shankaranarayana and D Arun Verma, who are serving life sentences for the December 2003 murder of Shubha’s 27-year-old fiancé, software engineer B V Girish, in Bengaluru.
The Cabinet held that the killing was premeditated and exceptionally brutal, and that the requests for clemency could not be accepted within the applicable legal framework.
“The recommendation will now be sent to Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot for a final decision on the petitions. The Home Department had obtained opinions from the police and prison departments before placing the matter before the Cabinet,” home minister Priyank Kharge said after the meeting on Thursday.
The petitions followed a July 14, 2025, Supreme Court judgment that upheld the life sentences imposed on all four people convicted in the case.
Dismissing their appeals, the court gave the convicts eight weeks to approach the governor under Article 161 of the Constitution, which empowers governors to grant pardons, suspend sentences, remit punishments or commute them in cases within the state’s executive jurisdiction. The Cabinet’s rejection does not constitute the governor’s final decision. The constitutional process will conclude when the governor decides the petitions.
Girish, a software engineer at Intel in Bengaluru, and Shubha, then a fifth-semester student of an integrated BA LLB course at BMS Law College, had got engaged on December 1, 2003, and their wedding was scheduled for April 11, 2004.
According to the prosecution case examined by the Supreme Court, Shubha was unwilling to marry Girish and wanted to pursue her relationship with Arun Verma, a fellow law student. Verma, then 19, was studying in the first semester of the same course.
On the evening of December 3, 2003, Shubha asked Girish to take her out for dinner. He picked her up from her home at around 6.30 pm on his scooter, and they went to TGI Friday’s, a restaurant near his workplace.
After dinner, the couple stopped at the Air View Point on Airport Ring Road to watch aircraft land. Between 9.30 pm and 9.40 pm, they informed their families that they had finished dinner and were returning home. At the viewing point, an assailant struck Girish on the head with a steel rod and fled.
Shubha, with the help of passers-by, stopped a car and took Girish to Manipal Hospital on Airport Road. He was declared dead at 8.05 am on December 4.
The prosecution alleged that the attack was part of a conspiracy to kill Girish because Shubha did not want to proceed with the marriage. Investigators subsequently arrested Shubha, Verma and two other men, A Venkatesh and Dinesh, also known as Dinakaran.
The Supreme Court’s 132-page judgment examined communications between the accused in the days leading up to the murder. Phone records showed frequent exchanges between Shubha and Verma before the killing, including communications on the day of her engagement to Girish.
The four accused had exchanged 56 communications on December 2, according to the judgment. On the evening of December 3, Shubha and Verma exchanged 38 text messages between 6.37 pm and 9.39 pm while she was out with Girish.
The court considered the volume and timing of these communications alongside evidence about the accused persons’ relationships, the recovery of the weapon and their conduct after the attack. It found that the prosecution had established the motive and the conspiracy.
The court also examined evidence that messages had been deleted from the accused persons’ phones. The communications, together with the other circumstances proved during the trial, formed part of the chain of evidence on which the convictions rested.
The trial court convicted all four accused in July 2010 and sentenced them to life imprisonment. The Karnataka high court upheld the sentences later that year. The Supreme Court subsequently examined their appeals and, on July 14, 2025, confirmed the convictions and life sentences.
Arun Dev is an Assistant Editor with the Karnataka bureau of Hindustan Times. A journalist for over 10 years, he has written extensively on crime and politics.

scraped_articles.title: ‘I am not missing anywhere’: Shraddha Dubey breaks silence on boyfriend Shiva Sharma’s death
scraped_articles.content:
Model and social media influencer Shraddha Dubey, who is wanted in connection with the death of Lucknow cafe owner Shiva Sharma, has denied reports that she is missing, claiming in a video statement released on Wednesday night that Sharma died by suicide and not murder.
Dubey said she intended to appear before the police to record her statement and disclose what happened. Her remarks came after the Lucknow police announced a reward of ₹ 25,000 each for information leading to the arrest of Dubey, her sister Rashmi and their driver in connection with Sharma’s death on October 9.
DCP (central) Vikrant Vir said the prime accused remained at large, with police teams sent to Delhi and the Nepal border following intelligence inputs about her possible escape routes.
In the purported video, Dubey said she wanted to cooperate with the police and urged the media not to link her to politicians or senior officials, claiming she had no involvement with them.
"I am not missing anywhere. I want to come to the police and give my statement. I want to tell them everything that is true,” Dubey can be heard saying in the video.
She also disputed the murder allegations surrounding Sharma’s death, describing the incident as suicide.
“Whatever is true regarding Shiva Sharma is that he was not murdered. It was a suicide,” she said.
The claims come as investigators examine CCTV footage that purportedly captures Sharma’s fatal fall from the fourth floor of Awadh Green Apartments in Lucknow’s Balu Adda area. The footage surfaced on Tuesday and is being examined to reconstruct the sequence of events and establish the roles of those present at the apartment.
Police have also questioned two to three people close to Dubey to gather details about her relationship with Sharma and the circumstances surrounding his death.
Sharma, 28, was found dead after falling from the apartment where he had allegedly been living with Dubey for around three to four months, as reported by HT earlier.
His mother, Ranjana Sharma, accused Dubey, her sister Rashmi and several others of assaulting, harassing and blackmailing her son before his death. Based on the complaint, Hazratganj police registered a murder case under Section 103(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).
According to the FIR, a copy of which HT has accessed, Dubey allegedly pushed Sharma from the fourth floor. His mother also claimed that his body bore cigarette-burn marks.
The post-mortem report cited multiple external injuries and extensive internal trauma, including damage to the lungs, liver and spleen. The cause of death was attributed to shock and haemorrhage.
While the findings establish the severity of Sharma’s injuries, they do not, by themselves, determine whether he was pushed, jumped or fell accidentally. Investigators will have to establish the circumstances surrounding his death through the available evidence.
Originally from Rae Bareli, Dubey built a public profile through modelling assignments, beauty pageants and fashion events. She reportedly won the ‘Best Face of Lucknow’ title and has around 1.41 lakh followers on Instagram, where her account, stylebookbyshraddha, features photographs and reels.
A music video featuring Dubey, released by a prominent music company around seven years ago, has reportedly garnered approximately 2.7 lakh views on YouTube.

scraped_articles.title: Kerala HC suspends 4-year jail term of former DGP in disproportionate assets case
scraped_articles.content:
The Kerala high court on Thursday suspended the four-year jail sentence awarded by a Vigilance court to former director general of police (DGP) Tomin J Thachankary in a disproportionate assets (DA) case.
“Prime facie, the finding of the learned Special judge could not be faulted in any manner. However, despite the objection raised by the State, this is a case in which the sentence imposed is only four years and in such view of the matter, the sentence can be suspended by imposing necessary conditions, in the interest of justice,” the high court bench of Justice A Badharudeen said.
As part of the conditions imposed by the court, the former DGP has been directed to deposit 75% of the fine imposed on him.
Thachankary, a 1987-batch Kerala-cadre Indian Police Service (IPS) officer, retired in 2023 as the DGP of Investigations at the State Human Rights Commission.
The former DGP was convicted by a Vigilance court in Kottayam in September this year for amassing wealth disproportionate to his known sources of income between 2003 and 2007. It was the first time an officer of DGP rank had been found guilty in a DA case.
He was awarded four years of rigorous imprisonment and fined ₹ 30.84 lakh.
The Vigilance judge had said in the order, “The higher the public office held, greater is the obligation to maintain the highest standards of integrity and probity. The disproportion of ₹ 30,84,892.39, constituting 52.33% of the known income, is neither marginal nor insignificant. It represents the unexplained enrichment accumulated during the check period from 2003 to 2007, when the said amount had substantial value.”
Vishnu Varma is Assistant Editor and reports from Kerala for the Hindustan Times. He has 10 years of experience writing for print and digital platforms and has worked at The New York Times, NDTV and The Indian Express in the past. scraped_articles.title: ‘Hot, fresh, good meals’: Delhi Police says October 10 detainees were treated with care, not lodged in jails
scraped_articles.content:
Those detained in view of October 10 protest in Delhi against the Election Commission of India (ECI) over alleged discrepancies were given food, tea, coffee and other refreshments and were not lodged in jails, the Delhi Police told the Supreme Court on Thursday.
In an affidavit, cops said that the detained leaders were accommodated in police station offices. Track live updates on Delhi protests
The Delhi Police made the claims in a counter-affidavit filed in response to contempt proceedings over alleged non-compliance with the Supreme Court’s directions on regulating public transport during the protest.
As stated in an earlier HT report , police said the detainees were released within a few hours, before the maximum 24-hour period contemplated under the relevant provisions; they were not lodged in police lock-ups or jails, were provided food and allowed to leave once the circumstances necessitating their removal had ceased.
Defending the move to deny permission for the CJP's anti-CEC protest at Jantar Mantar, Delhi Police commissioner Anurag Kumar reportedly said that people were removed under Section 65 of the Delhi Police Act and Section 172 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) only where Section 163 orders were in force.
Those removed were kept in "makeshift centres", given "hot, fresh and good meals" and let go within two to six hours, the affidavit adds. Political leaders were seated in SHO chambers and offered “tea, coffee, meals and other refreshments,” the Commissioner was quoted as saying in a Bar and Bench report.
Abhijeet Dipke-led CJP on had called for a protest against the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar on October 10 over the alleged SIR irregularities. However, the Delhi Police responded with a mass crackdown, detaining major leaders, including CJP's Dipke, Saurav Das and Abhijeet Ranka. The trio reached Delhi from Mumbai on the morning of October 10 and were picked up from the plane itself by Delhi Police personnel after it landed at the airport.
An estimated 7,000 people were detained , including four former chief ministers , MPs, student activists, social media influencers and civil society members.
The Delhi Police has also said the mass detentions ahead of the anti-CEC protest helped avert a ‘major public order situation’, HT reported earlier.
“A major public order situation was averted by timely, proportionate and lawful measures taken by the Delhi Police,” maintained the affidavit.
Commissioner Kumar described the detentions as “proportionate to the legitimate objective of maintaining law and order and preventing harm to persons and property”, adding that the police could not have allowed breach of public order by an organisation with a recent history of ‘mob violence, destruction of properties and incidents causing injuries to several people,’ referring to the Jantar Mantar clashes on July 20 during NEET exam row protests.
The police commissioner described the July 20 march by CJP over the NEET-UG paper leak as “unauthorised, unlawful and illegal”. The police have argued that those participating in the previous march were part of an unlawful assembly, seeking to justify the action taken against the mobilisation on October 10.
The commissioner sought to justify the restrictions by citing what he describes as CJP’s repeated disregard of police directions and the conditions imposed for public demonstrations. The affidavit says the organisation had given a written undertaking for an earlier protest in June, including assurances that the gathering would remain peaceful, would not exceed 1,000 participants and would not turn into a march towards Parliament without prior permission.
The police alleged that the undertaking was subsequently breached and that the organisation later mobilised people for an unauthorised march towards Parliament on July 20. These allegations concerning the July event led to the police’s decision to deny permission for the October 10 mobilisation, according to the affidavit.
(With inputs from Utkarsh Anand, Bar and Bench).

scraped_articles.title: Indian-origin woman arrested at Delhi airport for taking  ₹60 lakh to arrange German citizenship
scraped_articles.content:
Delhi Police have arrested a woman holding German citizenship for allegedly cheating a man of ₹ 60 lakh by promising to arrange permanent residency for him in Germany.
Poonam Jezler was arrested at Indira Gandhi International (IGI) Airport on Tuesday after a look-out circular (LOC) was issued against her, news agency ANI reported. Jezler's lawyer filed a bail application but later withdrew it following arguments.
She claimed to be the daughter of a former law secretary of Madhya Pradesh.
Jezler allegedly conspired with others to induce the complainant, Pranzal Kumar, to transfer ₹ 60 lakh to two of her bank accounts, the investigation found. She allegedly promised to arrange German citizenship or permanent residency for him.
Police said Jezler also introduced Kumar to a man named Rajat Arora, who allegedly claimed to work at the German Embassy. However, the promised citizenship or permanent residency was never arranged, and the money was not returned.
The police registered an FIR at Vasant Kunj police station in 2025 in connection with the case.
Seeking two days of police custody, the investigating officer told the court that the investigators needed to trace the money trail, identify other people allegedly involved in the conspiracy and verify whether any German Embassy official had a role in the case.
Police also sought to recover original documents, financial records and electronic devices that could contain communications between the accused and the complainant. The investigators said they needed to verify Jezler's claims about arranging German citizenship or permanent residency.
According to the police, they could not trace Jezler earlier because she is a German citizen and lives in Switzerland with her husband, who is a Swiss national. Investigators had also visited Mumbai to locate her children, but the address they had was found to be incorrect.
Police subsequently issued an LOC against her and froze her bank account, the investigating officer told the court.
The officer also informed the court that the police had notified the German Embassy, the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) and the Ministry of External Affairs about her arrest.
While granting police custody, the court noted that the transfer of ₹ 60 lakh into Jezler's bank accounts appeared to be undisputed. However, it said investigators needed to establish why the money was transferred and determine the accused's specific role in the alleged offence.
The court also said a detailed investigation was necessary to trace the money, identify other alleged conspirators and recover electronic devices that could contain incriminating communications with the complainant.
A court in Delhi on Wednesday remanded her to two days of police custody, till Friday, to investigate the alleged fraud. Jezler was produced before the Patiala House Court after spending a day in judicial custody.
Public Prosecutor Gagan Bhatnagar and advocate Shashwat, representing the complainant, opposed her bail plea.
Jezler is also the president of the World Book of Records, Switzerland, and was conferred the Bharat Kirti Chakra in 2022, according to the information presented in the case.
